parts.title: Multiple choice
parts.instructions: This examination paper has 50 multiple choice questions (1 to 50). Each question has 4 choices. Choose one best answer and blacken the letter of your choice on the separate answer sheet.

source.notes: Transcribed from the V-A text layer and checked against the page images. Bold and/or underlined emphasis words (does not, is not, wrong Statement, last, is true, was not) are kept as <u>…</u>. Figure 1 (two wells) and Figure 2 (river map with X and Z) were cropped from 300-dpi page renders. The events box for Q38-39 is an image on page 6 and was typed from the image. Tables 1-3 are given as tables.
source.printing_note: Misprints kept as printed: Q17 'It is rich is coral diversity'; Q26 'fron local ruler' and 'Jailbreaker of Nacfa' (the textbook says Nakura); Q42 'RN I'; Q50 option A printed 'A,' and 'Carabinnieri'. Table 3 leaves the Africa death rate blank on purpose (Q42).

questions.stem: The country that borders Eritrea in south-east is____
explanation_steps: Eritrea borders the Sudan in the west, Ethiopia in the south and Djibouti in the south-east. Yemen is across the Red Sea in the east (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 54).
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Djibouti is on the south-east side of Eritrea.
tips: West = Sudan, South = Ethiopia, South-east = Djibouti.

similar_questions.stem: Which country borders Eritrea in the west?
explanation_steps: The Sudan is in the west. Answer: C.

questions.stem: The activity of buying and selling is called _______
explanation_steps: Trade means buying and selling goods. Traders buy crops, fruit, fish and salt and sell them (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 98).
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Buying and selling is trade.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>does not</u> match?
explanation_steps: The textbook says: history textbooks are secondary sources. Stories told orally are also secondary sources (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 4).
Archaeological remains and pictures are primary sources. So only A is wrong. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: A history textbook is a secondary source, not a primary source.
tips: Primary = from the time itself. Secondary = written or told later.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a primary source?

options.C: A story told by a grandmother

explanation_steps: An old coin comes from the time itself. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> an active volcano?
explanation_steps: The textbook says some volcanoes are no more erupting, for example Emba Soira (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 121). Emba Soira is an extinct volcano.
Dubbi (erupted in 1400 and 1861), Alid and Dalloh are in the active volcanic area of the Danakil. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Emba Soira does not erupt any more.

similar_questions.stem: Mount Dubbi is a/an:
explanation_steps: Dubbi erupted in history. Answer: A.

questions.stem: In ancient times the most important trading port of Eritrea was____
explanation_steps: Goods coming from outside came to Adulis and were taken inland. Adulis exported ivory and tortoise shell (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 61–63).
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Adulis was the big old port.

similar_questions.stem: Adulis exported:
explanation_steps: Adulis exported ivory. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Change 1 : 1, 000, 000 to a scale statement
explanation_steps: 1 : 1,000,000 means 1 cm on the map = 1,000,000 cm on the ground.
1 km = 100,000 cm. So 1,000,000 cm ÷ 100,000 = 10 km (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 18).
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: 1,000,000 cm is 10 km. So 1 cm stands for 10 km.
tips: To change cm to km, divide by 100,000.

questions.stem: What century is 205 C.E,
explanation_steps: The years 1–100 C.E. are the 1st century, 101–200 the 2nd century and 201–300 the 3rd century (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 13).
205 is between 201 and 300. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: 205 C.E. is in the 3rd century.
tips: Take the hundreds number and add 1: 205 → 2 + 1 = 3rd.

similar_questions.stem: In which century is 1975 C.E.?
explanation_steps: 1901–2000 is the 20th century. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The landform in Eritrea between the highlands and lowlands is:
explanation_steps: Eritrea has three relief regions: the highlands, the escarpments and the lowlands (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 3–4).
The escarpments are the steep slopes between the highlands and the lowlands. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The steep land between highlands and lowlands is the escarpment.

similar_questions.stem: Eritrea can be divided into highlands, escarpments and:
explanation_steps: The third region is the lowlands. Answer: B.

Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Queen Hatshepsut of Egypt sent ships to Punt.

similar_questions.stem: Queen Hatshepsut was a queen of:

questions.stem: Well A is empty. Well B has water. Both are the same well at different part of the year in Eritrea. The cause for the rise and lowering of the groundwater is due to……..
questions.image_alt: Figure 1: two drawings of the same well. Well A (dry period): the water table is below the bottom of the well, so the well is empty. Well B (rainy period): the water table is higher, so the bottom of the well has water. Under the water table is saturated rock.

options.C: The seasonal nature of the rainfall

explanation_steps: It is the same well. So the rocks and the landform do not change.
Well B is in the rainy period and Well A is in the dry period. The textbook says the groundwater rises in the rainy season and becomes low in the dry period (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 23).
So the change comes from the seasons of rain. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: In the rainy season the water table goes up. In the dry season it goes down.
tips: Same well, different season → the cause is the season (rain).

similar_questions.stem: In the rainy season the water table:
explanation_steps: Rain water seeps into the ground. Answer: B.

questions.stem: A disaster brought by the consequence of human activities is_____
explanation_steps: The textbook says: man-made disasters are war, pollution, deforestation, erosion etc. (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 113).
Lightning, tides and storms come from nature. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Erosion is made worse by people, for example when they cut trees.
tips: Man-made disasters: war, pollution, deforestation, erosion.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a man-made disaster?
explanation_steps: War is made by people. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>does not</u> match?
explanation_steps: Buildings, roads and factories are made by people. They are not natural.

Drought, epidemics and earthquakes are disasters (Grade 7, p. 113). Adulis, Kohaito and Metera are cultural heritage (Grade 7, p. 91). Corals, dugong and mangroves are natural heritage (Grade 7, p. 95). Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Buildings, roads and factories are made by people, so they are not a natural environment.
tips: Natural = made by nature. Buildings = made by people.

similar_questions.stem: Which is part of the natural environment?
explanation_steps: A river is natural. Answer: C.

options.A: It is rich in terrestrial plants
options.B: it is rich in fish diversity
options.C: It is rich is coral diversity

explanation_steps: Terrestrial means 'on land'. The sea has marine life, not land plants.
The Red Sea has over one thousand kinds of fish and many corals (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 95). It is very salty. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Terrestrial plants grow on land, not in the sea.

similar_questions.stem: Which one lives in the Red Sea?
explanation_steps: The dugong is a sea animal. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following dates comes <u>last</u>?
explanation_steps: B.C.E. dates are before C.E. dates. So 1500 B.C.E. and 700 B.C.E. come first.
Among C.E. dates, the bigger number is later: 1000 C.E. is after 900 C.E. (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 13–14). Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: 1000 C.E. is the latest date.
tips: B.C.E.: bigger = older. C.E.: bigger = newer.

similar_questions.stem: Which date comes first?
explanation_steps: 300 B.C.E. is the oldest. Answer: A.

questions.stem: The wrong statement is _______

options.B: Plants take in CO₂ and give out oxygen at day time
options.D: At night plants take in oxygen and give out CO₂.

explanation_steps: Minerals such as gold, copper and salt are non-renewable. They cannot reproduce (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 82–84).
Soil is renewable if we use it carefully. Plants take in CO₂ in the day and give out CO₂ at night. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Minerals cannot make new minerals. They are non-renewable.
tips: Minerals = non-renewable. Plants, animals, soil, water = renewable.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a non-renewable resource?
explanation_steps: Copper is a mineral. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: The branch of government which makes laws is
explanation_steps: The textbook: the legislature is the law-making body; the executive makes decisions and carries them out; the judiciary judges (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 85).
Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: The legislative branch makes the laws.
tips: Legislative = makes laws. Executive = acts. Judiciary = judges.

similar_questions.stem: The branch of government that judges cases is the:

similar_questions.stem: Fishing is a ___ activity.

explanation_steps: Early people kept animals around them and this led to cattle breeding (domestication of animals) (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 65).

questions.stem: Which area is rich in groundwater?
explanation_steps: The textbook: places with alluvial soils have a large amount of groundwater (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 23–24).
Limestone and sandstone areas in Eritrea have poor groundwater, and impermeable rocks do not let water in. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Alluvial soils hold a lot of groundwater.
tips: Alluvial soil = soil brought by rivers; water goes in easily.

similar_questions.stem: Which place has a large amount of groundwater?
explanation_steps: Hazemo has alluvial soils. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs <u>does not</u> match ?

options.A: Mahdist Revolt → Movement to liberate Egypt from foreign control
options.C: Giuseppe Sapeto → Bought Assab fron local ruler
options.D: Ali Muhammad Usman Burri → “Jailbreaker of Nacfa ’’

explanation_steps: The Mahdi led the movement to liberate the Sudan (not Egypt) from foreign control (Social Studies Grade 8, p. 68–69).
The Italians were defeated at Dogalli in 1887 and Sapeto bought Assab (p. 74–76).
Note: the textbook calls Burri the 'jail-breaker of Nakura' (p. 78), not of Nacfa. We take this as a small slip. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: The Mahdist Revolt was in the Sudan, against Egypt.

questions.stem: In the caste system,

options.A: People of the same social position, occupation, wealth and influence are grouped together
options.B: There are no differences in wealth and social position

explanation_steps: The textbook: in the caste system society was divided into levels; each level had people of the same occupation, social position and influence (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 73). So A is true.
In a caste system people are born into their caste; the position passes from parents to children. So C is true too. B is false. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: People of the same job and position are grouped, and children keep the same caste.
tips: Caste = fixed level you are born into.

questions.stem: Which statement is true ?

options.A: The Mahdi was a deputy of Muhammad Ali
options.B: Muhammad Ali was a ruler of the Turks in early 19th century
options.C: The Naibs represented Turkish interests in Massawa
options.D: Ali Abu Gassim led the anti-Egypt revolt in the Sudan

explanation_steps: The Turks ruled the coast through the Naib; the Naib was their deputy (Social Studies Grade 6, p. 71). So C is true.
Muhammad Ali was the ruler of Egypt (Grade 8, p. 68). The Mahdi (Muhammad Ahmad) led the revolt in the Sudan against Egypt. Answer: C.

questions.stem: In social development the one which represents the higher stage is________

The Grade 7 book covers primitive communal to feudal; capitalism comes after feudalism. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Capitalist society comes after feudal society, so it is higher.

explanation_steps: The textbook says slave society was the first class society. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which one <u>is true</u> of system of government?

options.A: In a unitary system of government all power is concentrated in a central government
options.B: In a federal system states are basically independent but cooperate in certain ways
options.C: In a Confederation , power is concentrated in a central government
options.D: In a federal system no power is given to local government

explanation_steps: The textbook: in a unitary state (like Eritrea) the central government decides all major policies (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 86). So A is true.

In a federal system the national and regional governments share power, so B and D are wrong. States that are independent but cooperate form a confederation, where the centre is weak, so C is wrong. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: In a unitary system, the central government has the main power.
tips: Unitary = one centre. Federal = shared power.

similar_questions.stem: Eritrea has a ___ system of government.
explanation_steps: Eritrea is a unitary state. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.subject: Social Studies

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs <u>does not</u> match ?

options.D: Diessa-------system with village ownership of land

explanation_steps: The textbook: endas joined together to make villages; clusters of villages made a gulti; gultis formed a medri (Social Studies Grade 7, p. 138).
So an enda is a small family group, not a cluster of medri. The Diessa system is village ownership of land (p. 137). Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Endas are small. They are not groups of medri.
tips: Enda → village → gulti → medri (small to big).

similar_questions.stem: Gultis together formed a:
explanation_steps: Gultis formed a medri. Answer: B.
